_note: Campaign roster for cymbal_voyages.campaign_history and ad_performance. Dates are fixed calendar dates. daily_spend_usd is the paid budget per day summed across the campaign's markets (before seasonal multipliers). bookings_attributed and roi are the numbers the brand corpus briefs quote; ad_performance.attributed_conversions is scaled to agree with them. roi = (attributed_revenue * 0.22 contribution margin - budget) / budget.

segments.all_customers: Everyone in the CRM, members and non-members
segments.prospects: Anonymous and first-time visitors with no account
segments.lapsed_compass_cold: Cymbal Compass members in cold-weather markets with no booking in 12+ months
segments.lapsed_compass: Cymbal Compass members, any market, with no booking in 12+ months
segments.active_compass: Cymbal Compass members who booked in the last 12 months
segments.ski_enthusiasts: Customers who viewed or booked ski destinations
segments.adventure_seekers: Customers who viewed or booked adventure destinations
segments.cruise_interest: Customers who viewed or booked cruise itineraries
segments.urban_explorers: Customers who viewed or booked city breaks

campaigns.name: Always-On Brand Search
campaigns.retrospective: Steady performer that mostly captures customers who already decided to book with us. Cost per booking has crept up 9% year over year as competitors bid on our name. Kept on because turning it off in a 2024 test cost measurable bookings.

campaigns.name: Warm Escapes Retargeting
campaigns.objective: Re-engage lapsed Compass members in cold-weather markets who browsed warm destinations
campaigns.retrospective: Our always-on paid-social program for members who browsed a warm destination but did not book. Historically our most efficient always-on program, because it reaches people who already told us what they want. Budget was rotated to Fall City Breaks in late July 2026 to fund the launch.

campaigns.name: Winter Sun Early Bird 2025
campaigns.objective: Win back lapsed Compass members ahead of the winter warm-escape season
campaigns.retrospective: Bonus Compass points for booking a warm escape by October 31, sent to lapsed members with a warm, no-pressure tone. Beat its booking target by 31% and brought 1,960 members back at a contribution ROI of 4.3. Members told us in the post-campaign survey that points felt like recognition; a discount would have felt like a coupon.

campaigns.name: Holiday Gift of Travel 2025
campaigns.objective: Drive gift bookings and holiday-season trips
campaigns.retrospective: Broad seasonal push with gift-card and family-package creative. Landed close to plan at a 2.6 ROI. Family-pool imagery outperformed everything else in this window, which we now attribute to the season more than the segment.

campaigns.name: New Year Ski 2026
campaigns.objective: Fill January and February ski inventory
campaigns.retrospective: Search-led campaign against a defined intent audience. Efficient at 2.9 ROI; adventure-style imagery of the mountain beat lodge imagery by a wide margin. Ran short of premium inventory in Jackson Hole in week four.

campaigns.name: Spring Flash Sale 2026
campaigns.objective: Lift a soft March with a sitewide 15% discount
campaigns.retrospective: Fifteen percent off everything, to everyone, with urgency messaging. Bookings came in 40% under target and the discount consumed most of the margin on the ones we did get, for a contribution ROI of -0.4. Compass members converted worse than non-members, and the post-mortem concluded the sale cheapened the brand for exactly the customers who value it most.

campaigns.name: Wave Season Cruises 2026
campaigns.retrospective: Search plus email to customers who had viewed an itinerary. Solid 2.4 ROI; the Alaska Inside Passage itinerary sold out its June departures by the end of February.

campaigns.name: Summer Adventure 2026
campaigns.objective: Sell summer adventure itineraries to active travelers
campaigns.retrospective: Video-first paid social with real itinerary footage. Delivered a 2.7 ROI and our best-ever engagement rate on paid social. Iceland and Patagonia carried the campaign; the national parks package underperformed against its forecast.

campaigns.name: Compass Anniversary Double Points
campaigns.objective: Reward active members during the program's anniversary month
campaigns.retrospective: Email-only, double points on any booking in June, to active members. Very efficient at 8.5 ROI because the audience was already warm and the only cost was points and production. Confirms that points move members more than price does.

campaigns.name: Affiliate Partner Program
campaigns.objective: Commission-based bookings through travel content partners
campaigns.retrospective: Pay-on-booking partnerships with travel publishers. Predictable and low-risk, though partner bookings skew to first-time customers who rarely join Compass.

campaigns.name: Last-Minute Warm Deals 2026
campaigns.objective: Move remaining February and March warm-escape inventory
campaigns.retrospective: Free-night framing on unsold February departures, to active members in cold and mild markets. Cleared the inventory at a 3.4 ROI. Free-night offers read as generous without teaching customers to wait for a discount.

campaigns.name: Fall City Breaks 2026
campaigns.objective: Launch the fall city-break category with a full-funnel paid-social push
campaigns.retrospective: Funded by rotating the always-on paid-social budget rather than new money. Through mid-September it has delivered 640 bookings at roughly break-even, with city-skyline creative performing well against urban explorers. Too early to call, and the retargeting program it displaced has not been restored.
